name: Pear and Quince Marmalade
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: sugar to each 1 lb. fruit
ingredients.originalText: 1 1/2 lbs. sugar to each 1 lb. fruit

ingredients.name: water to each lb. sugar
ingredients.originalText: 1 pt. water to each lb. sugar

instructions.text: Weigh fruit after it is ready to cook
Pare and core the fruit and throw into cold water
Stew parings and cores in a little cold water to make syrup
When the parings are well boiled strain off liquid
When cold put in fruit and bring quickly to a boil, boiling until smooth
Add the sugar and lemon juice, and cook steadily for an hour
Work with a spoon to a rich jelly

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Weigh fruit after it is ready to cook
2. Pare and core the fruit and throw into cold water
3. Stew parings and cores in a little cold water to make syrup
4. When the parings are well boiled strain off liquid
5. When cold put in fruit and bring quickly to a boil, boiling until smooth
6. Add the sugar and lemon juice, and cook steadily for an hour
7. Work with a spoon to a rich jelly
originalIngredients: 1 1/2 lbs. sugar to each 1 lb. fruit
1 pt. water to each lb. sugar
